English and AI

Add a Database to Your App with an AI Agent

Some apps need to save data, for example votes, scores, or photos. Your agent can create a database and storage for your app and connect them to it. But a few steps need you. This guide shows those steps in order.

Your service
1234567

Before you start

You need these three things.

  • Your app. It does not need to be deployed yet. You can add a database before the deployment, or together with it.
  • A CloudflareVercel account and a token for the agent. If you do not have a token yet, follow the deploy guide to make one, and add D1 Edit in step 4 of this guide.
  • A clear idea of the data that your app needs to save. For example: votes, quiz scores, or photos.

Steps in this guide

  1. Ask your agent to add a database
  2. Check the plan
  3. Read what the agent needs
  4. Add D1 Edit to your token
  5. Turn on R2 (only for photos or files)
  6. The agent creates the database
  7. Check your data and your usage
  1. Ask your agent to add a database
  2. Check the plan
  3. Read what the agent needs
  4. Create the Neon database
  5. Create the Blob store (only for photos or files)
  6. The agent deploys the app
  7. Check your data and your usage
1

Ask your agent to add a database

Send this prompt to your agent. Change the words in brackets to the data of your app.

Your prompt

I want to use Cloudflare for this app. I want to save [the number of votes and the photos that users upload]. Create a database or storage for this data, and connect it to my app. Before you create anything, explain your plan: which services you will use, and what data you will save in each one.

Note
On Cloudflare, the agent will probably suggest D1 for data such as votes and scores, and R2 for photos and other files. You do not need to decide this yourself. Talk with the agent, and ask questions, for example: Why do we need this? or Is it free?
2

Check the plan

The agent explains its plan first. The plan says which service keeps each kind of data. In a database, the data is kept in tables, and each table has columns.

The agent might show

Here is my plan.

  • D1 (database): table votes with id (number) and count (number), and table photos with id (number), file_name (text), and created_at (time)
  • R2 (storage): the photo files. The table photos keeps only the name of each file.

The photos will be private. Only your app can show them.

Read the plan before the agent creates anything. Check these points.

  • Every piece of data in the plan is something that your app really uses.
  • There is no column for passwords. If your app has a login, ask the agent to use a safe login method.
  • There are no student ID numbers or phone numbers, unless your app really needs them.
  • The plan says whether the photos are public or private. Anyone who has the address of a public photo can open it.

If something is wrong, tell the agent and ask for a new plan. If the plan is fine, send this prompt.

Your prompt

The plan is fine. Please create it.

3

Read what the agent needs

If the agent chose D1, it needs one more permission. The token from the deploy guide can already use R2. But it cannot make a D1 database, because it does not have the permission D1 Edit.

The agent might ask

I cannot create the D1 database. The token does not have the permission D1 Edit. Please add D1 Edit to the token.

To save photos in R2, please also turn on R2 in your Cloudflare account.

This table shows where each setting is on the screen.

The agent might sayOn the Cloudflare screen
D1 Edit, or D1 WriteYour token, then Account policy. Search for D1 and click the box Edit.
Turn on R2, or enable R2The page R2 Object Storage, the button Add R2 subscription to my account
Note
You add the permission to the same token. You do not need a new token, and the file cloudflare_token.txt stays the same.
4

Add D1 Edit to your token

Open dash.cloudflare.com. Click the person icon at the top right, then Profile, then API Tokens. Click a picture to see it bigger.

5

Turn on R2 (only for photos or files)

Do this step only if your app saves photos or other files. You do it one time for each Cloudflare account. Open your account. In the left menu, click Storage & databases, then R2 Object Storage.

Be careful
R2 needs a payment method, for example a credit card. If your account has no card, Cloudflare asks for one on this page. You pay only if you use more than the free amount. If you do not want to register a card, talk with your instructor before this step.
Note
If you see a list of buckets and not this page, R2 is already on. Skip this step.
6

The agent creates the database

Go back to the agent and send this prompt.

Your prompt

I added D1 Edit to the token, and I turned on R2. Please continue.

The agent might say

I created the D1 database and the R2 bucket, and I connected them to the app. I deployed the app. Your app is here:

https://your-app-name.your-subdomain.workers.dev

Open the link. Use the part of your app that saves data, for example vote one time. Then reload the page. If the data is still there, the database works.

7

Check your data and your usage

You can see your data and how much you used on the Cloudflare website.

Your data in D1

Your files in R2

The free limits

ServiceFree amount
D1 storage5 GB for each account
D1 rows read5 million each day
D1 rows written100,000 each day
R2 storage10 GB each month
Be careful
The D1 limits are for each day. If your app reaches a limit, it cannot read or save data until 9 a.m. Korean time. The data that you saved does not disappear.
Your prompt

Check that this app stays within the free limits of D1 and R2.

Later

  • You want to save new kinds of data. Ask the agent: Before you change anything, explain your plan.
  • You test your app. Use fake data, for example Test User 1. Do not use the data of real people.
  • The project is finished. Open the token page again and delete the token.
1

Ask your agent to add a database

Send this prompt to your agent. Change the words in brackets to the data of your app.

Your prompt

I want to use Vercel for this app. I want to save [the number of votes and the photos that users upload]. Create a database or storage for this data, and connect it to my app. Before you create anything, explain your plan: which services you will use, and what data you will save in each one.

Note
On Vercel, the agent will probably suggest a Neon database for data such as votes and scores, and Vercel Blob for photos and other files. You do not need to decide this yourself. Talk with the agent, and ask questions, for example: Why do we need this? or Is it free?
2

Check the plan

The agent explains its plan first. The plan says which service keeps each kind of data. In a database, the data is kept in tables, and each table has columns.

The agent might show

Here is my plan.

  • Neon (database): table votes with id (number) and count (number), and table photos with id (number), url (text), and created_at (time)
  • Vercel Blob (storage): the photo files. The table photos keeps only the address of each file.

The photos will be private. Only your app can show them.

Read the plan before the agent creates anything. Check these points.

  • Every piece of data in the plan is something that your app really uses.
  • There is no column for passwords. If your app has a login, ask the agent to use a safe login method.
  • There are no student ID numbers or phone numbers, unless your app really needs them.
  • The plan says whether the photos are public or private. Anyone who has the address of a public photo can open it.

If something is wrong, tell the agent and ask for a new plan. If the plan is fine, send this prompt.

Your prompt

The plan is fine. Please create it.

3

Read what the agent needs

Vercel does not make its own database. The database comes from another company, Neon, through the Storage page of Vercel. The agent may ask you to create it on the website.

The agent might ask

Please create a Neon database in the Storage tab of your Vercel project, and connect it to this project.

For the photos, please also create a Blob store.

This table shows where each setting is on the screen.

The agent might sayOn the Vercel screen
Neon, or Postgres databaseYour project, then Storage, then Create Database, then Neon
Connect it to the projectThe window Connect a Project at the end
Blob storeYour project, then Storage, then Create Database, then Blob
Private, or PublicAccess in the window Create Blob Store
Note
Some agents can create the database by themselves. If your agent does not ask you, skip steps 4 and 5.
4

Create the Neon database

Open vercel.com and click your own project. Click a picture to see it bigger.

Note
When you connect, Vercel adds the connection information to your project as environment variables. You do not need to copy it.
5

Create the Blob store (only for photos or files)

Do this step only if your app saves photos or other files. Open Storage again and click Create Database.

Be careful
With Public, anyone who has the address of a file can open it. Do not use Public for photos of people or for private documents.
6

The agent deploys the app

Vercel uses the new environment variables only after a deployment. Go back to the agent and send this prompt.

Your prompt

I created the database and connected it to the project. Make the tables, and deploy to production.

The agent might say

I made the tables and deployed the app to production. Your app is here:

https://your-app-name.vercel.app

Open the link. Use the part of your app that saves data, for example vote one time. Then reload the page. If the data is still there, the database works.

7

Check your data and your usage

You can see your data and how much you used on the Vercel website. Open Storage and click your database or your Blob store.

Your data in Neon

Your files in Blob

The free limits

ServiceFree amount
Neon storage1 GB for each project
Neon compute time100 CU-hours for each project
Blob storage1 GB each month
Blob data transfer10 GB each month
Note
When nobody uses the Neon database for 5 minutes, it stops. The next request wakes it up in about one second, so the first answer after a break can be a little slow.
Your prompt

Check that this app stays within the free limits of Neon and Blob.

Later

  • You want to save new kinds of data. Ask the agent: Before you change anything, explain your plan.
  • You test your app. Use fake data, for example Test User 1. Do not use the data of real people.
  • The project is finished. Open the token page again and delete the token.
The websites sometimes change their screens. These pictures are from November 2026. If a button is in a different place, find the same word on the screen.
